window_duration_ms is the hard-coded WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30_000, unrelated to the data scored (last 60 prosodic events via SERIES_MAXLEN) or to the triggering snapshot's own window_duration_ms (60_000 in dynamics.py). Per-speaker deques are appended only when that speaker's PROSODIC_FEATURE arrives, and timestamp_ms is discarded. `_pearson_clamped` and the CRQA/TE calls then tail-align `a[-n:]` with `b[-n:]`, treating index i of A as simultaneous with index i of B. With diarized speakers who alternate turns, that pairing is arbitrary, so attentiveness, coordination and symmetry are not measuring temporal coupling. Store (timestamp_ms, value) and align on timestamps, or at least document the assumption. `dynamics.py` has the same limitation, but this component's scores depend on the alignment more directly.

A pair with little data does not get a neutral score. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 when it has fewer than 10 samples, and `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` returns 1.0, so the first snapshots report perfect symmetry. Missing `f0_mean` is appended as 0.0 (unvoiced frames or an absent key), which feeds fake zeros into CRQA and TE and inflates both. Gate symmetry and coordination on a minimum sample count, or skip those components, and don't append defaults for absent keys.

Three hand-rolled per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0) duplicate `SpeakerTimeSeries`, which `GroupDynamicsEngine` already uses to hold per-speaker prosodic features and expose f0 series and speaker ids. Reuse it, or extend it with arousal/valence getters. Otherwise there are two accumulators with different retention rules (60 samples here, 120 s there). The `series_dict`/`key`/`default` tuple loop in `_handle_prosodic` is also harder to read than it needs to be.

`WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30_000` is a hard-coded constant that matches neither the data nor the trigger. The data is the last 60 samples (`_series_maxlen`), whatever their duration. The upstream snapshot already carries `window_duration_ms` (60 s in `dynamics.py`), and the engine ignores it. Derive the value from the snapshot payload, or from the actual retained span.

Existing engines are exported from `forgestream/emotion/__init__.py` and attached through `Orchestrator.attach_*` methods (`attach_dynamics_engine`, `attach_emotion_correlator`). RapportEngine has neither, so nothing can subscribe `on_event` to the EventBus. The `rapport_*` config fields already exist for this. Add the export and an `attach_rapport_engine` that reads those config fields.

`weights_applied` is rounded to 4 decimals per key, so the emitted weights can sum to something slightly off 1.0, while the spec says they sum to 1.0. Emit the unrounded values, or round only for display.

Insufficient data inflates rapport. With too few samples (or flat f0), compute_transfer_entropy returns 0 for both directions and compute_symmetry returns 1.0 (perfect symmetry). Positivity defaults to 0.5, so a pair with no evidence scores about 0.3 composite under the meeting-1 weights. This biases group_composite and group_trend upward in the first snapshots. Treat symmetry as 0.0 when the series are too short to estimate TE.
interpolate_weights: math.exp(-(meeting_count - 3)) raises OverflowError for very negative meeting_count (roughly below -700). Clamp meeting_count first.

`_compute_trend` returns Pearson correlation of recent composites vs time index. It is bounded to [-1,1] regardless of change size, so a 0.500 -> 0.502 drift gives ~1.0. The spec's example (0.03 on a 0.68 composite) and its downstream `rapport_trend > 0.1` rule imply a slope in score units. Use the regression slope per snapshot (np.polyfit(idx, y, 1)[0]) and drop the std guard.

Symmetry is 1.0 whenever both transfer entropies are ~0. That covers series shorter than 11 samples (compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0) and constant or unvoiced f0. It adds 0.20-0.25 weight of free credit to early composites, while coordination is 0 for the same data (router returns 0 below 10 samples). Gate symmetry on a minimum series length or return a neutral or 0 value when there is no signal.
`_f0_series` duplicates the per-speaker f0 history that `SpeakerTimeSeries` already keeps. `RapportEngine` is also not exported from `forgestream/emotion/__init__.py`, unlike the sibling engines.

_compute_trend returns the Pearson correlation of recent composites against their index, which is scale-free. A near-flat noisy series gives about ±1. The spec's example is group_trend 0.03 and the planned consumer uses 'trend > 0.1' as a threshold, which suggests a slope. Use a slope (e.g. np.polyfit) or document that correlation is intended.
_compute_pair_rapport is typed dict[str, object], so sum(p["composite"] ...) in _handle_snapshot fails type checking. Use a TypedDict or dataclass for the pair score.

_compute_trend returns Pearson r of composites vs time index, which saturates near ±1 for any monotone drift regardless of magnitude. The spec example is group_trend 0.03, and the trust region fires on rapport_trend > 0.1. Use a slope (e.g. np.polyfit) so the value is a magnitude, or change the spec and thresholds.

_handle_prosodic appends f0_mean even when it is 0.0, which PraatExtractor emits for unvoiced windows. Zeros flow into CRQA and transfer entropy, inflating %DET from constant stretches and skewing TE binning. Skip or treat unvoiced frames as missing for the F0 series.

With too little data, compute_symmetry(0, 0) returns 1.0 and _valence_proximity falls back to 0.5. A fresh pair gets about 0.2 composite from symmetry alone, plus positivity, so early scores overstate rapport. Return 0 for symmetry when the series are too short for TE (compute_transfer_entropy needs at least 10 points).

_compute_pair_rapport calls CRQAComputeRouter.compute once per pair, sequentially. The breaker counts failures and skips per call, but its 5-cycle skip assumes one call per 60s cycle. With 3 speakers one failing snapshot opens the circuit and the skip is spent in under 2 snapshots. A dead endpoint also blocks the handler for up to 4s × pairs. Gather concurrently or make the breaker per-snapshot.

Sibling engines have attach_* helpers in orchestrator.py and are exported from emotion/__init__.py. RapportEngine has neither, so nothing subscribes it to the EventBus. Add attach_rapport_engine and the export.
The ±50 exponent clamp in interpolate_weights guards a case that doesn't occur (math.exp overflows only below about -709). Drop it.

window_duration_ms reports 30s, but the series are bounded by event count (SERIES_MAXLEN=60) and not reset per snapshot, so the reported window doesn't match the data scored. Window by timestamp_ms or document the approximation.

Raw Hz F0 lists go to CRQAComputeRouter.compute. Only _local_compute z-scores; _runpod_compute posts them raw with radius=0.25. The spec requires z-scored log-F0. With a RunPod endpoint set, coordination will be near 0 or meaningless and will differ from the local path. Normalise before calling the router.
Unvoiced windows have f0_mean=0.0 (features.py). _handle_prosodic appends these zeros to _f0_series, and they feed CRQA and transfer entropy as real pitch values. Skip or mask unvoiced samples.

With fewer than 10 points compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0, and compute_symmetry(0,0) returns 1.0. Early snapshots therefore give every pair full symmetry credit from no data, while attentiveness is 0.0 for the same situation. Treat insufficient data as neutral or as no signal.

SERIES_MAXLEN=60 is an event count, not a time window. window_duration_ms just echoes the snapshot payload or defaults to 30000. Attentiveness correlates the tails of two non-time-aligned series by index. Window by timestamp or document the approximation.
Not wired in. Sibling engines have Orchestrator.attach_* methods and are exported from emotion/__init__.py. RapportEngine has neither, so nothing subscribes it to the EventBus.
Hand-rolled per-speaker deques duplicate what SpeakerTimeSeries already provides (timestamped per-speaker features, get_f0_series, speaker_ids).
The exponent clamp in interpolate_weights guards math.exp overflow for extreme meeting_count but has no comment explaining that.

With insufficient data the composite is inflated. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0 for both directions on short or flat series (<12 samples), so `compute_symmetry` returns 1.0. `_valence_proximity` returns 0.5 for empty series. The first snapshot after a few events therefore scores about 0.35 (0.20*1.0 + 0.15*0.5 at meeting 1) with no evidence, and this feeds `group_composite` and `group_trend`. Gate symmetry on a minimum series length, and ideally skip or flag the pair.

The payload reports `WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30000`, and the spec says the components are computed over a 30-second window. The series use `deque(maxlen=60)`, about 60s at one event per second, so the reported window does not match the data used. Align the maxlen (about 30) or report the real window.

`_compute_trend` returns Pearson r vs index, which is in [-1, 1] and saturates on tiny monotone drifts. The spec example `group_trend: 0.03` looks like a slope. Pick one meaning and document it in the docstring.

`_handle_prosodic` appends `f0_mean` for every PROSODIC_FEATURE event. `features.py` emits `f0_mean: 0.0` for unvoiced or silent windows, so those zeros go into `_f0_series`. They then feed `crqa_router.compute` (coordination) and `compute_transfer_entropy` (symmetry). That makes %DET and symmetry reflect silence patterns instead of pitch coordination, and `_discretize` z-scores the zeros as real values. Skip unvoiced frames (f0_mean <= 0), or keep per-speaker series that exclude them. The design spec's pipeline also z-scores log-F0, which this does not do.

`_pearson_clamped` aligns the two arousal deques by tail index (`a[-n:]`, `b[-n:]`), not by timestamp. Each speaker's series only grows when that speaker produces an event, so in turn-taking speech sample i of A and sample i of B are not simultaneous. The correlation is therefore not 'tracking' in the time sense the spec describes. At minimum document the assumption. Better, store `(timestamp_ms, value)` and resample onto a common grid.

The payload reports `window_duration_ms=30000`, but `_series_maxlen=60` keeps up to ~60 samples, and the comment calls that '~60 seconds'. The reported window and the data actually used disagree. Derive both from one constant, or fix the comment.

`disengagement_damped` is computed as `damping < 1.0`. With `damping_factor >= 1.0` it reports False even when a speaker is flagged. Use `self._disengagement.is_disengaged(sp_a) or self._disengagement.is_disengaged(sp_b)` so the flag states what it means.

Symmetry reads 1.0 when there is no data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 for short or constant series (fewer than ~12 samples), and `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` then returns 1.0. A pair with no evidence therefore gets full symmetry credit: 0.20–0.25 weight, so a composite of at least ~0.2 with attentiveness and coordination at 0. The early-meeting group composite and `group_trend` are inflated. Treat 'insufficient data' as 0.0 (or skip the component) instead of perfect symmetry.

Pair metrics align the two speakers' series by tail index, not by timestamp. `_pearson_clamped` uses `a[-n:]` and `b[-n:]`. The f0 series passed to CRQA and transfer entropy are also compared by position. Speakers produce different numbers of chunks, so sample k of A is not simultaneous with sample k of B, which weakens attentiveness, coordination and symmetry. `timestamp_ms` is already in each prosodic payload, so the series could be time-aligned.

`coordination = _clamp01(crqa.det)` ignores `crqa.surrogate_validated`. The design spec says that if the synchrony is not significant, coordination should be 0.0. Without a RunPod endpoint, `_local_compute` always returns `surrogate_validated=False`. Raw unvalidated %DET then feeds the heaviest weight from meeting 5 on, while the payload only flags it as `surrogate_validated: false`. Either gate it or note that the local fallback is deliberately ungated.

`_handle_prosodic` keeps three per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0). `SpeakerTimeSeries` in `emotion/speaker.py` already buffers per-speaker prosodic payloads and has `get_f0_series`; `GroupDynamicsEngine` uses it. Two parallel buffering implementations will drift, for example in max length and the default for a missing f0.

`window_duration_ms` is the hard-coded constant 30_000. The series are bounded by sample count (`_series_maxlen = 60`), not time. The incoming ENTRAINMENT_SNAPSHOT carries its own `window_duration_ms` (60_000). The reported window therefore does not correspond to the data used. Derive it or pass it through.

`_handle_snapshot` awaits `_compute_pair_rapport` serially for each pair. `EventBus.publish` awaits handlers one by one, so a degraded RunPod endpoint can block the bus for up to `runpod_timeout` × number of pairs per snapshot. The circuit breaker only opens after 3 failures. Running the pair computations with `asyncio.gather` would bound this to one timeout.

Sibling engines are exported from `emotion/__init__.py` and have an `Orchestrator.attach_*` helper (`attach_emotion_correlator`, `attach_dynamics_engine`). `RapportEngine` has neither, so nothing in the app can subscribe it yet. This is fine if wiring is a planned follow-up.

WINDOW_DURATION_MS is hardcoded to 30_000, but snapshots arrive every 60s (SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS in dynamics.py) and the series are deque(maxlen=60) of events, not a time window. The emitted window_duration_ms misdescribes the data. Echo the triggering snapshot's window_duration_ms or compute the actual span.

Symmetry inflates composites on thin data. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for short or constant series, and compute_symmetry(0,0) returns 1.0, so a pair with almost no data gets symmetry 1.0 at 0.20-0.25 weight while attentiveness and coordination are 0. Gate symmetry on a minimum series length, as the CRQA router does with its <10 guard.

group_trend is a Pearson correlation of composites against the time index, not a slope. It is scale-free, so tiny jitter gives values near +/-1. The design spec example (0.03) and the planned rapport_trend > 0.1 trust-region threshold suggest a per-window change. Use a least-squares slope or document the choice.

The three parallel per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0) duplicate SpeakerTimeSeries in emotion/speaker.py, which already accumulates per-speaker prosodic features and exposes get_f0_series and speaker_ids. Reuse it for a single source of truth.
logger is defined but never used; remove it and the logging import.
A missing f0_mean defaults to 0.0 and is appended to the F0 series, so missing or unvoiced frames become real zeros in CRQA and transfer-entropy input. Skip the sample when the key is absent.

_handle_prosodic appends arousal, valence and f0 independently and skips missing values per series, so a speaker's three series can drift out of alignment. setdefault runs before the None check, so a speaker with no usable fields still counts as 'known' and satisfies the two-speaker gate, then scores ~0 on most components. Gate speaker discovery on a speaker actually having data, and append the three values together or not at all.

The three parallel per-speaker deque dicts duplicate SpeakerTimeSeries, which GroupDynamicsEngine already uses (speaker_ids(), get_f0_series()). Consider SpeakerTimeSeries(max_duration_seconds=30) to avoid a second per-speaker series convention and the hard-coded 1 Hz SERIES_MAXLEN assumption.
"RapportEngine" is inserted before "PraatExtractor" in __all__, breaking the alphabetical ordering. It belongs after "ProsodicFeatures".

With <10 samples or constant F0, TE is 0 for both directions, so compute_symmetry returns 1.0 (perfect symmetry) and positivity defaults to 0.5. This adds ~0.2-0.25 to the composite from no data and skews group_composite and group_trend early in a session. Gate symmetry/coordination on sufficient samples or use a neutral/zero default.

_pearson_clamped aligns the last n entries of each speaker's deque by index, but entries are only appended when that speaker has an event with a non-None value. The series are not time-aligned across speakers, and the arousal, valence and F0 deques can differ in length. Attentiveness correlates mismatched samples. Align on timestamp_ms or document the approximation.

SpeakerTimeSeries already maintains rolling per-speaker prosodic series and is used by GroupDynamicsEngine. This adds three parallel dict[str, deque] stores with their own maxlen logic instead of reusing or extending it.
"RapportEngine" is inserted before "PraatExtractor" in __all__, breaking the alphabetical ordering of the list.

Pair series are paired by position, not time. `_aligned_tail`, `_attentiveness`, `_coordination` and `_symmetry` take the last N samples per speaker, but speakers append only on their own events, so sample i of A and sample i of B are not simultaneous. Arousal correlation, CRQA and TE then compare unrelated moments. `_coordination` also drops unvoiced frames per speaker before aligning, while `_symmetry` keeps zeros, so the two components use different F0 series. Align by timestamp_ms or document the approximation.

No `attach_rapport_engine`. Siblings (`attach_emotion_correlator`, `attach_dynamics_engine`) each have an attach method that creates the handler and subscribes it. Without one nothing subscribes the engine, so RAPPORT_SCORE is never emitted in the real pipeline.

`window_duration_ms` is a hard-coded 30000, and the comment says '1 per second', but samples arrive per PROSODIC_FEATURE event. The upstream snapshot's `window_duration_ms` (60000) is ignored. The reported value can be wrong. Derive it from the timestamps in the window or from the snapshot.

Three parallel dicts (`_arousal`, `_valence`, `_f0`) are kept in sync by hand. `SpeakerTimeSeries` already stores timestamped per-speaker feature dicts. Reuse or extend it, or use one per-speaker structure.

Symmetry returns 1.0 (perfect) when TE is 0, which includes every pair with fewer than ~12 samples because `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0. A pair with almost no data gets full symmetry credit, inflating early composites. Attentiveness defaults to 0.0 for undefined, so the defaults are inconsistent. Gate on a minimum sample count.

`_handle_snapshot` awaits `_score_pair` sequentially inside the bus handler. With a RunPod endpoint each pair can wait up to `runpod_timeout`, so delay grows with N(N-1)/2 pairs and stalls the bus. Consider `asyncio.gather` across pairs.
The `try/except Exception` around `self._router.compute` duplicates the router's own RunPod failure and local fallback. It also hides local-compute bugs behind a warning. Narrow it or drop it.
The `self._score_pair(...)` call in `_handle_snapshot` is over-long. The quoted `"Orchestrator"` annotation is redundant under `from __future__ import annotations`.

`window_duration_ms` is hard-coded to `WINDOW_SAMPLES * 1000` (30000), and the comment assumes 1 sample/second. The ENTRAINMENT_SNAPSHOT that triggers the computation already carries `window_duration_ms` (60000 from `GroupDynamicsEngine`), and PROSODIC_FEATURE cadence isn't guaranteed to be 1 Hz. The reported duration can be wrong. Take it from the snapshot payload, or derive it from the actual sample timestamps.

`_symmetry` returns 1.0 (perfect symmetry) whenever there is not enough data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 below 10 samples or on constant series, and `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` returns 1.0. Early in a meeting, or with flat F0, every pair gets full symmetry credit (0.20–0.25 of the composite) with no evidence. Also, `_symmetry` runs TE on raw F0 including unvoiced zeros, while `_coordination` drops `f0 <= 0` frames, so the two components treat the same data differently. Consider neutral/0 symmetry when TE is undefined, and filter unvoiced frames consistently.

`_handle_snapshot` awaits `self._router.compute` sequentially per pair inside the EventBus handler. With a RunPod endpoint configured, each pair can block up to `runpod_timeout` (4s), so N speakers means N(N-1)/2 × 4s of handler latency. The local fallback is also synchronous CPU work on the event loop. Consider `asyncio.gather` over the pairs.

Sibling engines (`attach_emotion_correlator`, `attach_dynamics_engine`) have `attach_*` helpers that subscribe `on_event` to the EventBus. This PR adds none for `RapportEngine`, so nothing subscribes it. Add `attach_rapport_engine` if wiring is meant to be part of this change.
The `await self._score_pair(sp_a, sp_b, weights, tlcc.get(frozenset((sp_a, sp_b))))` line in `_handle_snapshot` exceeds the line length used elsewhere. Pull the TLCC lookup into a local variable.

Symmetry defaults to 1.0 when data is insufficient. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for <10 samples or flat f0, and compute_symmetry(0,0) returns 1.0. Pairs with no f0 data therefore get full symmetry credit (+0.20-0.25 composite), inflating group_composite early in a session. Use a neutral or zero value when TE is uninformative.

window_duration_ms is hardcoded to 30000. GroupDynamicsEngine snapshots carry their own window_duration_ms (60 s interval), and the 60-sample deques match neither. Take it from the snapshot payload or derive it from the data actually scored.

Builds parallel per-speaker arousal/valence/f0 deques although SpeakerTimeSeries already accumulates per-speaker prosodic series. Extend SpeakerTimeSeries (add arousal/valence getters) instead of a second store.

Arousal tails are aligned by sample index, not timestamp, and missing arousal/valence silently becomes 0.5 and enters the correlation as fabricated data. Same approximation as dynamics.py, but note it in a comment/docstring and consider skipping missing values.

group_trend is a Pearson correlation vs time index (range [-1,1], no magnitude), while the spec example (0.03) looks like a slope. Document the choice or use a slope; likewise note why coordination uses raw det even when surrogate_validated is False.

`window_duration_ms` is hardcoded to 30000. `GroupDynamicsEngine` emits snapshots every `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000` and puts the real value in its snapshot payload as `window_duration_ms`, so the emitted RAPPORT_SCORE reports the wrong window. Read it from `event.payload.get("window_duration_ms", ...)` and drop the constant, or import `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` from `dynamics`.

The engine keeps its own per-speaker arousal, valence and f0 deques alongside `GroupDynamicsEngine`'s `SpeakerTimeSeries`, which already stores per-speaker prosodic features and has `get_f0_series`. The new deques are small, so this is acceptable. Pearson attentiveness compares the last n samples of each speaker by index, not by timestamp. Speakers' samples are not concurrent, so the correlation is only approximate. A short comment on that limitation would help the next reader.

_compute_trend returns the Pearson correlation of recent composites against the time index. It is scale-free: a monotone rise of 0.01 per window scores about 1.0, the same as a rise of 0.2 per window. The spec example (group_trend 0.03) and the downstream 'trend > 0.1' trust-region use imply a slope or delta. Use a least-squares slope so the magnitude means something.

_handle_prosodic appends float(p.get('f0_mean', 0.0)) to the F0 series. Unvoiced chunks already carry f0_mean=0.0 (features.py fallback). Those zeros feed CRQA and transfer entropy as real samples, which inflates coordination during shared silence and distorts z-scoring. Skip unvoiced or missing f0 instead of defaulting to 0.

Per-speaker deques are compared by tail length (_pearson_clamped) or front truncation (compute_transfer_entropy), not by timestamp. A late-joining or sparse speaker is paired with samples from different moments. The spec also requires enough data (30s) from both speakers before a pair is scored. A pair is currently scored as soon as two speakers exist. Gate on a minimum sample count per speaker or align by timestamp.
The `if not a or not b: return 0.5` branch in _valence_proximity is unreachable, because _handle_prosodic always appends to all three series together. Remove it.

disengagement_damped is computed as `damping < 1.0`. With damping_factor=1.0, a pair containing a disengaged speaker is reported as not damped. Derive it from membership of sp_a/sp_b in the disengaged set.

Symmetry defaults to 1.0 when there is no data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 for fewer than 10 aligned samples or flat series, and `compute_symmetry` maps TE of 0 on both sides to 1.0. A pair with too little history, or with unvoiced f0 of 0.0, therefore gets perfect symmetry and a free 0.20–0.25 composite boost. Treat insufficient-data TE as neutral (for example 0.5) or as 0, not as perfect symmetry.

Sample alignment is inconsistent. `_pearson_clamped` aligns from the tail (`a[-n:]`), but `compute_transfer_entropy` truncates both series from the head (`[:n]`). When the two speakers have different sample counts, TE and symmetry are computed on misaligned samples. Trim both f0 series to the same trailing window before the CRQA and TE calls.

`_handle_prosodic` builds three parallel per-speaker deque dicts for data that `SpeakerTimeSeries` already accumulates. Consider extending that class with arousal and valence accessors instead of keeping a second accumulator.

`compute_symmetry` returns 1.0 when both transfer entropies are 0, which happens with fewer than about 12 samples or with constant F0. A pair with no TE evidence gets full symmetry credit (0.2 of the composite at meeting 1). Treat the no-data case as neutral or 0.
`disengagement_damped` is computed as `damping < 1.0`. With `damping_factor=1.0` a disengaged pair reports False. Derive it from `is_disengaged(a) or is_disengaged(b)`.

`asyncio.gather` over all pairs shares one `CRQAComputeRouter`. With a RunPod endpoint, every pair's request is in flight before any failure is counted, so the circuit breaker cannot prevent a burst of N(N-1)/2 timeouts. Score pairs sequentially.

Three parallel per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0) duplicate the accumulator role of the existing `SpeakerTimeSeries` used by `GroupDynamicsEngine`. Consider reusing it instead of a second tracking structure.

`interpolate_weights` re-normalises, but both profiles already sum to 1.0. `weights_applied` is rounded to 4 places and may not sum exactly to 1.0. `list(pair_scores)` copies a list that `gather` already returned.
`Orchestrator` has `attach_*` helpers for the correlator and dynamics engine, but none for `RapportEngine`. The issue does not ask for one, so nothing subscribes this engine to the EventBus yet.

symmetry is 1.0 whenever there's no usable data. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for fewer than about 11 samples, and compute_symmetry(0, 0) returns 1.0. A pair with almost no history gets the full 0.20 symmetry weight, which inflates early-meeting composites. Consider neutral or 0.0 symmetry when both TE values are 0.

RapportEngine is never subscribed to the EventBus. Sibling engines (synthesis, correlator, dynamics) each have an attach_* method on Orchestrator. Without an attach_rapport_engine, nothing runs on_event outside manual wiring. Add one if the engine is meant to run in the pipeline.

_track_prosodic keeps its own per-speaker F0 deque, which duplicates what SpeakerTimeSeries does for GroupDynamicsEngine. Sharing it is possible, but the extra arousal/valence tracking makes a separate store acceptable.

Per-speaker series are paired by sample count (a[-n:] with b[-n:]), not by timestamp. Turn-taking speakers get compared on non-simultaneous samples, which weakens the Pearson (attentiveness), CRQA and TE (symmetry) components. Align on timestamp_ms, or document the limitation.

With insufficient or flat data, TE returns 0 for both directions and compute_symmetry(0, 0) returns 1.0. Positivity likewise defaults to 0.5. Sparse pairs therefore get the full symmetry weight (0.20 to 0.25) with no evidence, which inflates early composites. Treat the insufficient-data case as 0.0 or skip the pair.

_handle_snapshot awaits _compute_pair_rapport serially. Each call can wait up to runpod_timeout (4 s), so N speakers can block the EventBus handler for N(N-1)/2 x 4 s. It also consumes the router's circuit-breaker skip counter once per pair rather than once per snapshot. Use asyncio.gather or compute CRQA once per snapshot.

group_trend is Pearson r of the composite vs the time index, which is scale-free. A tiny steady drift reads near 1.0, and the spec example (0.03) looks like a slope. Pick a slope or an r and document it.
The _clamp01 on group_composite is redundant, because every pair composite is already clamped.

Symmetry is wrong when there is no data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 for both directions when there are fewer than ~11 voiced F0 samples (its `m < 10` guard). `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` then returns 1.0. During the first ~10 s, or whenever speakers are mostly unvoiced, every pair gets symmetry=1.0, which adds the full symmetry weight (0.20–0.25) to the composite. Coordination is 0 in the same case because CRQA also bails at fewer than 10 samples. Gate symmetry on sufficient data and score it 0.0 (or neutral) when TE is undefined, instead of reporting perfect mutual influence.

F0 series are appended only for voiced frames (`f0 > 0`), so the two speakers' log-F0 lists differ in length and are no longer time-aligned. `compute_transfer_entropy` truncates both with `[:n]` (the heads), while `_pearson_clamped` aligns the tails (`[-n:]`). Within one pair the components therefore use different alignment conventions. TE on head-truncated, misaligned series is close to meaningless. Pick one alignment, preferably the tails (most recent), and apply it to the log-F0 lists before CRQA and TE.

The engine keeps its own per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0), which duplicates what `SpeakerTimeSeries` already does (rolling per-speaker prosodic features). `GroupDynamicsEngine` already uses `SpeakerTimeSeries`. Consider using it with a 30 s window plus small accessors for arousal and valence, instead of a second accumulation convention.

`GroupDynamicsEngine` is exported from `forgestream/emotion/__init__.py` and wired through `Orchestrator.attach_dynamics_engine()`. `RapportEngine` has neither the export nor an attach path. `config.py` already defines `rapport_enabled`, `rapport_damping_factor`, `runpod_crqa_endpoint` and `runpod_timeout_seconds`, and nothing reads them. The engine is never subscribed, so it never runs outside tests. At minimum add the `__init__` export. The attach helper is probably the intended follow-up; say so explicitly.

The `interpolate_weights` docstring says meeting 1 is ~90% early profile and 5+ is ~90% established. The sigmoid gives about 88% at meeting 1 (t≈0.12) and 88% at meeting 5 (t≈0.88). Say ~88%, or drop the number.

The `SERIES_MAXLEN` comment says ~1 Hz gives a 30 s window, and `WINDOW_DURATION_MS` is a separate hard-coded 30_000. Derive one from the other so they can't drift. The snapshot interval itself is 60 s in `dynamics.py`.

`compute_symmetry` returns 1.0 when both transfer entropies are ~0, and `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 when it has too few samples. A pair with little or no f0 data therefore gets `symmetry == 1.0`, contributing 0.20–0.25 to the composite for no reason, while coordination is 0. Early in a session rapport is inflated. Gate symmetry on sufficient f0 data and return a neutral or 0 value otherwise.

The series aren't time-aligned. Arousal and valence get one sample per event. f0 is appended only when `f0_mean > 0`, so the f0 series are shorter and differ between speakers. Pearson compares tails, but CRQA and transfer entropy get the raw lists (`compute_transfer_entropy` truncates from the head). Index n of speaker A is not time-matched to index n of speaker B, and the alignment convention differs across components. Align by timestamp or document the approximation.

Pairs are scored one at a time with `await` in a list comprehension. With a RunPod endpoint each pair can wait up to `runpod_timeout` (4 s), and pair count grows as N(N-1)/2, so the EventBus handler can block a long time. Use `asyncio.gather` over the pairs, after checking the router's circuit-breaker state is safe under concurrent calls.

Sibling engines have `Orchestrator.attach_emotion_correlator()` and `attach_dynamics_engine()` plus exports in `emotion/__init__.py`. `RapportEngine` has neither, and nothing subscribes it to the EventBus, so it never runs in the app. Add `attach_rapport_engine` and the export, or confirm wiring is a separate change.

Unvoiced frames (f0<=0/missing) are dropped from the F0 series, but arousal and valence get a sample on every event. CRQA and transfer entropy then get F0 lists of different lengths per speaker that are no longer time-aligned across speakers. Attentiveness also aligns the two speakers' tails by index, not timestamp. Store (timestamp, value) and align by time, or keep the F0 series aligned and mask the unvoiced frames.
`logger` is defined but never used. Remove it, or log the skipped snapshot when there are fewer than two speakers.

Unvoiced F0 samples are dropped while arousal and valence are always appended, so each speaker's F0 series is sampled differently. TE (`compute_transfer_entropy`) and CRQA pair these series by index. Tail-aligning series of different lengths gives misaligned pairs. Document this limitation, or forward-fill the unvoiced samples.
`_compute_pair_rapport` returns bare `dict`. A `TypedDict` for the pair-score entry would document the payload shape.

Per-speaker arousal/valence/f0 deques are appended per event with no timestamp alignment, and the pair scores never use timestamp_ms. Pearson, CRQA and transfer entropy therefore pair the last n samples of each speaker by position, not time. Mismatched speaking rates compare different moments. Align by timestamp or document the one-event-per-tick assumption.

Re-implements per-speaker prosodic accumulation (_arousal_series, _valence_series, _f0_series) when SpeakerTimeSeries in emotion/speaker.py already does this (add_feature, get_f0_series, speaker_ids). Extend and reuse it. Otherwise there are two accumulators with different retention (60 entries vs 120 s).

coordination = clamp(crqa.det) uses raw %DET even when surrogate_validated is False (always the case on the local fallback). The design spec says non-significant synchrony should score 0.0 or be compared to a noise floor. Unvalidated recurrence can inflate the composite. If deliberate for now, say so in a comment.
`logger` and `import logging` are unused. Remove them.

`_compute_pair_rapport` aligns unequal-length per-speaker series inconsistently. `_pearson_clamped` takes the last `n` samples (`a[-n:]`). `compute_transfer_entropy` truncates from the head (`src[:n]`, `tgt[:n]`), and `crqa_router._local_compute` builds a full cross-recurrence matrix over the unequal series. So attentiveness and symmetry score different sample windows for the same pair. Each series also only grows when that speaker emits a prosodic event, so index alignment isn't time alignment. Trim both f0 lists to a common tail length once in `_compute_pair_rapport` before the CRQA and TE calls, or document the limitation.

`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30_000` disagrees with `GroupDynamicsEngine`, which emits snapshots every `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` (60 s) and always includes `window_duration_ms`. The fallback is wrong if it is ever used. Import the dynamics constant or drop the default.

`_compute_trend` returns a Pearson correlation against the time index, which is in [-1, 1] and ignores magnitude. A tiny noisy upward drift gives about +0.9. The design spec example (`group_trend: 0.03`) and the planned 'trend > 0.1' threshold imply a slope in composite units per snapshot. Use the slope from `np.polyfit(x, y, 1)`, or document the correlation choice.

Three parallel per-speaker deques (arousal, valence, f0) drop timestamps, so two speakers' series are aligned only by tail index. `GroupDynamicsEngine` pairs its series the same way. A single per-speaker deque of `(timestamp_ms, payload)` would be simpler and allow time-based alignment.
`logger` and `import logging` are unused. Remove them or log RunPod fallback or disengagement transitions.

Per-speaker arousal, valence and f0 are kept in three new dict-of-deque structures. `SpeakerTimeSeries` in `speaker.py` already accumulates per-speaker prosodic features and `GroupDynamicsEngine` uses it. Reuse or extend it instead of adding a second accumulator.

Arousal Pearson and the f0 CRQA/transfer-entropy inputs pair the tails of the two speakers' deques by count, not by timestamp. Diarized speakers emit at different times, so the pairs are not simultaneous samples. The deques hold up to 60 samples, but `window_duration_ms` reports 30000 or the snapshot's value. Align on `timestamp_ms`, or at least document the limitation.
`logging` and `logger` are imported and defined but never used. Remove them.
`group_trend` is a Pearson correlation against the time index, so it is about ±1 for any monotone run whatever the magnitude. The payload field name does not say this. Document it or return a slope.

Pairs with too little data score as if they had good rapport. `compute_symmetry` returns 1.0 when both transfer entropies are 0, and `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0 for short or constant series. A pair with one or two samples (or all-zero f0) therefore gets symmetry=1.0 and positivity=0.5 by default, so its composite is about 0.35 with no evidence. Suppress or neutralise symmetry when either series is too short for transfer entropy. Alternatively, skip pairs with fewer than N samples.

Attentiveness and coordination pair the per-speaker deques by index tail (`a[-n:]`, `b[-n:]`). Each deque only grows when that speaker has an event, so index i for A and index i for B are not the same moment. The Pearson and CRQA inputs are not time-aligned. The 60-sample cap also does not match the 30 s window the spec describes for attentiveness. `GroupDynamicsEngine` has the same limitation, but a rapport measure should not copy it unchanged. Either align by `timestamp_ms` or document the approximation.

`_handle_prosodic` keeps its own per-speaker deques, duplicating `SpeakerTimeSeries` (`speaker.py`), which already accumulates per-speaker prosodic payloads and exposes `get_f0_series`. Extending that class with arousal and valence getters would avoid a second accumulator and the duplicated default handling (`f0_mean` defaulting to 0.0, which also injects fake unvoiced samples into the F0 series).

`logger` is defined but never used. `_clamp01(group_composite)` is redundant because each pair composite is already clamped. `weights_applied` is rounded to 4 decimals, so the emitted weights may not sum exactly to 1.0 even though `interpolate_weights` does. Consider emitting them unrounded.
DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS = 60_000 duplicates SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS in dynamics.py, the source of the snapshot's window_duration_ms. Import that constant instead of redefining it.

Three parallel dicts (_arousal_series, _valence_series, _f0_series) keyed by the same speaker IDs, with _arousal_series doubling as the speaker registry. Use one per-speaker structure, or extend SpeakerTimeSeries, which already stores f0_mean per speaker, so the invariant is not implicit.

Series alignment is inconsistent when speakers have different sample counts. `_pearson_clamped` uses the tails (`a[-n:]`). `compute_transfer_entropy` truncates to the head (`src[:n]`). `crqa_router.compute` gets the unequal lists untouched. Until both deques are full, attentiveness, coordination and symmetry use different windows. Trim both lists to a common tail once in `_compute_pair_rapport` and pass the trimmed lists to all three.

The engine keeps three parallel per-speaker `dict[str, deque]` structures with its own `maxlen` of 60. `SpeakerTimeSeries` (`emotion/speaker.py`) already accumulates per-speaker prosodic features and is what `GroupDynamicsEngine` uses, with a 120-entry window. Extend it with arousal and valence getters instead of adding a second per-speaker series convention.
`logger` is defined but never used. The `.crqa_router`, `.disengagement` and `.transfer_entropy` imports sit after the `TYPE_CHECKING` block; group them with the other imports.

Symmetry rewards missing data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 when it has fewer than 10 lagged samples. `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` then returns 1.0, so a pair with almost no history gets full symmetry. At meeting 5 that adds about 0.25 to the composite. Only compute symmetry when there is enough data, or return a neutral value such as 0.5 or 0.0 when both TEs are 0 because of too little data. Otherwise early snapshots are inflated and the group trend is biased.

`_compute_trend` returns the Pearson r of composites against the time index, which is scale-free. A composite moving 0.600 to 0.601 to 0.602 gives a trend of 1.0. The design spec's consumers act on thresholds like `rapport_trend > 0.1`, and with a correlation almost any monotone noise clears that. Use the least-squares slope per snapshot, or document that this is a correlation.

The engine keeps its own per-speaker arousal, valence and f0 deques, with `_series_maxlen=60`. `SpeakerTimeSeries` in `emotion/speaker.py` already accumulates per-speaker prosodic features, and `GroupDynamicsEngine` uses it for the same f0 series. Use or extend it, for example with arousal and valence getters, instead of a second accumulator with different retention. The 60-event cap also ignores the 30 s window that the payload's `window_duration_ms` reports.

Sibling engines (`EmotionCorrelator`, `GroupDynamicsEngine`) are re-exported from `forgestream/emotion/__init__.py`. `RapportEngine` is not. The relative imports also sit after the `TYPE_CHECKING` block, which is odd import ordering.

Symmetry is 1.0 when there is no evidence. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 for fewer than 10 samples or constant series, and `compute_symmetry` maps total TE ~0 to 1.0. A pair with only a few prosodic events therefore gets a free 0.20–0.25 of composite weight. Treat insufficient data as neutral or 0, e.g. by checking the series length or both TEs ~0 before calling `compute_symmetry`, rather than as perfect symmetry.

`coordination = _clamp01(crqa.det)` ignores `surrogate_validated`. The design spec says coordination is 0 when CRQA is not significant. The RunPod path zeroes `det` itself, but the local fallback (the default with `runpod_endpoint=""`) returns raw unvalidated `det`. That unvalidated value then carries up to 0.40 of the composite. Either gate or discount it when `surrogate_validated` is False, or document that the local path is deliberately ungated.

Not integrated the way sibling engines are. There is no `Orchestrator.attach_rapport_engine()` (cf. `attach_dynamics_engine`, `attach_emotion_correlator`) and no export in `forgestream/emotion/__init__.py`. Without these nothing subscribes `on_event` to the EventBus.

Per-speaker arousal, valence and f0 deques duplicate state that `SpeakerTimeSeries` already keeps, including `get_f0_series`. Consider reusing it, adding arousal and valence getters, instead of three parallel dicts with a hardcoded maxlen of 60.

_handle_prosodic appends f0_mean=0.0 (what features.py emits for unvoiced windows) into _f0_series. Those zeros feed CRQA and transfer entropy and can fake or distort coordination and symmetry. Skip non-positive f0_mean for the F0 series. The spec also calls for z-scored log-F0 per speaker, which is not done.

_series_maxlen=60 (~60 s) doesn't match the payload's window_duration_ms, which defaults to 30_000, and the spec says the components are computed over the 30 s window. The reported window can differ from the data actually scored. Align the two or derive the length from the snapshot.

Symmetry is 1.0 when there is no evidence. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for short or constant series, and compute_symmetry maps total<1e-10 to 1.0. A pair with fewer than ~11 samples therefore gets perfect symmetry, adding 0.20-0.25 to the composite, while coordination is 0 for the same data. Treat insufficient data as 0.0 or skip the pair instead of reporting perfect symmetry.

WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30000 is a hardcoded constant. The series hold ~60 samples and snapshots arrive every 60 s (dynamics.SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS), and the snapshot payload already carries window_duration_ms. 30000 matches the spec example, but add a comment or forward the snapshot value.

`window_duration_ms` is hard-coded to 30000, but the series deque holds 60 samples (the comment says ~60 s). The triggering snapshot also carries its own `window_duration_ms` (`SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` in `dynamics.py`). The reported window therefore doesn't match the data actually scored. Either size `_series_maxlen` to the reported window or take the value from the snapshot payload. Name the 60 as a constant.

`_handle_prosodic` appends a fabricated default when a key is missing (`f0_mean` 0.0, arousal and valence 0.5). A missing or unvoiced `f0_mean` of 0.0 goes into the F0 series that feeds CRQA and transfer entropy, and constant 0.5 values flatten the Pearson and valence terms. If `p.get(key)` returns None, the later `np.array(..., dtype=float64)` calls will fail. Skip a series update when the value is absent or None.
`logger` is defined but never used. Remove it, or log the pair-compute and RunPod-fallback paths.
The sibling engines (`GroupDynamicsEngine`, `EmotionCorrelator`) are re-exported from `forgestream.emotion`. `RapportEngine` is not added to `__init__.py` or `__all__`.

group_trend is a Pearson r of composites vs. time index, which is scale-free: negligible drift gives about ±1. The spec's group_trend example (0.03) and its `trend > 0.1` threshold imply a slope per snapshot. Use a least-squares slope (np.polyfit) so the value carries magnitude.

coordination = _clamp01(crqa.det) uses the raw local det when surrogate_validated is False. The RunPod path returns 0.0 for non-significant results, but the local fallback has no noise floor, so chance recurrence counts as coordination at full weight. The spec says unvalidated synchrony should not count. Discount or zero it, or document the optimism.

Per-speaker deques only grow when that speaker has a PROSODIC_FEATURE event. _pearson_clamped, CRQA and transfer entropy then compare the trailing n samples of two series that can come from different moments. Align on timestamp_ms, or note the limitation.

Re-implements per-speaker rolling accumulation (_arousal_series, _valence_series, _f0_series) when emotion/speaker.py already has SpeakerTimeSeries with a max duration, get_f0_series and speaker_ids. Reuse it (30 s window, 1 s stride) or explain why not.

Other emotion engines are exported from emotion/__init__.py and have Orchestrator.attach_* helpers, which live_stream uses. RapportEngine has neither, so nothing in the running system produces RAPPORT_SCORE. Add the __init__ export now; the attach_rapport_engine() wiring the spec lists can follow.

WINDOW_DURATION_MS = 30_000 is hard-coded and only implicitly tied to SERIES_MAXLEN = 30 (one entry per second). The incoming snapshot's own window_duration_ms is 60,000. Add a comment linking the two constants.
`logging` and `logger` are imported and defined but never used. Remove them.

With too little data, `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0 (needs >=10 lagged samples) and `compute_symmetry(0,0)` returns 1.0. Symmetry then reads as perfect with no evidence. Positivity also defaults to 0.5 with no valence data. Early snapshots therefore get a sizeable composite from no signal. Gate symmetry/coordination on a minimum series length (or emit 0/neutral) until enough samples exist.

Missing or unvoiced f0 is stored as 0.0 and fed to CRQA and transfer entropy as if it were real pitch. `PraatExtractor` emits f0_mean=0.0 for unvoiced windows, so zeros distort the coordination and symmetry components. This mirrors `SpeakerTimeSeries`, but skipping unvoiced samples (or documenting the behaviour) would be safer.

Hand-rolled per-speaker deques (arousal/valence/f0) duplicate what `SpeakerTimeSeries` in `emotion/speaker.py` already does for f0 and energy. Reuse or extend it instead of keeping a parallel accumulator.

Sibling engines are exported from `emotion/__init__.py` and have `attach_*` helpers on Orchestrator. `RapportEngine` has neither, and the existing `rapport_*` config fields are unused. Optional, since the issue only asks for the class.

Symmetry returns 1.0 (perfect) when there is too little data, because compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for short or flat series and compute_symmetry maps a total under 1e-10 to 1.0. A pair with almost no history therefore gets full symmetry credit, up to 0.25 of the composite at meeting 5+. CRQA already returns det=0 for short series, so the components treat missing data inconsistently. Score symmetry as 0.0 or neutral when the history is below the TE minimum.

_track stores 0.0 when arousal, valence or f0_mean is absent from the payload. Zeros pull down mean attentiveness and positivity, and an unvoiced frame (f0_mean=0.0) pollutes the F0 series used for TE and CRQA. Skip absent keys instead of defaulting them.
Unused `logging` import and `logger`. `_mean` is missing a type annotation.

Attentiveness and positivity are not pairwise measures. `attentiveness` is the mean of both speakers' arousal and `positivity` is the mean of both speakers' valence. Two loud, upbeat speakers who never react to each other get a high score. A calm, well-synchronised pair gets a low one. The repo spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-29-rapport-tracking-design.md, Components 1 and 2) defines attentiveness as `max(0, pearson_r(arousal_a, arousal_b))` and positivity as `1 - |mean_valence_a - mean_valence_b|`. Implement the relational measures. They also keep the output in [0, 1] without relying on the clamp.

Coordination ignores surrogate validation. The spec (Component 3) says coordination is the normalized %DET only when it is significant, otherwise 0.0. The code uses `crqa.det` unconditionally and `crqa.surrogate_validated` only for reporting. The local fallback has no surrogate test, so its DET on noise or on constant F0 inflates coordination. That component carries the highest weight from meeting 5 on. `abs(f0_correlation)` also scores anti-phase F0 as coordination, which is inconsistent with the spec's treatment of negative correlation. Gate on significance, or document the chosen fallback.

Missing keys default to `0.0` in `_track` (`payload.get(key, 0.0)`). `correlator.py` defaults arousal and valence to `0.5`. A prosodic event without `arousal`, `valence` or `f0_mean`, or with an unvoiced `f0_mean` of 0, drags the means down. It also injects zeros into the F0 series fed to CRQA and transfer entropy. Skip missing or unvoiced samples, or use the neutral default. Also, `compute_symmetry` returns 1.0 when transfer entropy is 0, which includes the insufficient-data case. A pair with too little history therefore gets a perfect symmetry score.

`_score_pair` is awaited sequentially for every pair, and each call can wait up to `runpod_timeout` (4s by default) on RunPod. With N speakers there are N(N-1)/2 pairs, so a slow endpoint stalls this EventBus handler for a long time before the circuit breaker opens. Use `asyncio.gather` over pairs.

Symmetry is 1.0 when there is no data. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for short or constant series (fewer than 11 aligned samples), and compute_symmetry(0, 0) returns 1.0. Early in a meeting, or with unvoiced f0, a pair gets full symmetry credit (weight 0.20–0.25) with no evidence, which inflates the composite. Gate on a minimum sample count or use a neutral or zero value when TE is undefined.

Cross-speaker series are aligned by sample index (a[-n:] with b[-n:]) rather than by time. Speakers talk in turns and each deque fills at its own rate, so the paired samples are not simultaneous. Attentiveness, CRQA coordination and TE are therefore computed on misaligned data. Use event timestamps (SpeakerTimeSeries stores them) or a common time grid.

Three parallel per-speaker deques (_arousal_series, _valence_series, _f0_series) re-implement what SpeakerTimeSeries already provides (per-speaker rolling storage with timestamps and get_f0_series), as GroupDynamicsEngine uses it. Reuse it instead of a second convention.
A missing f0_mean is stored as 0.0, and unvoiced frames also report f0_mean of 0.0. These zeros feed straight into CRQA and TE and distort them. Mask or skip unvoiced and missing samples.

The inline default `0.5 if key != "f0_mean" else 0.0` in _handle_prosodic is hard to read. Put the default in the (dict, key, default) tuple. Also, `logger` is unused and `import math` precedes `import logging`.

Siblings have Orchestrator.attach_emotion_correlator and attach_dynamics_engine, but there is no attach_rapport_engine, so nothing subscribes the engine to the bus. Optional, since the issue does not ask for it.

Symmetry scores full credit when there is no data. `compute_transfer_entropy` returns 0.0 when there are fewer than ~11 samples. `compute_symmetry(0, 0)` then returns 1.0. A new pair therefore gets symmetry = 1.0 (weight 0.20–0.25), which inflates early composites. Return 0.0 or neutral when either series is too short for TE. Attentiveness and coordination already return 0 in that case.

Per-speaker series are appended only when that speaker emits an event. `_pearson_clamped` pairs `a[-n:]` with `b[-n:]` by tail index, not by time, so the pairing is arbitrary. The same applies to the f0 series fed to CRQA and TE. Store `timestamp_ms` with each sample and align on it. `SpeakerTimeSeries` already carries timestamps and could be reused.

Missing keys are filled with invented values: arousal and valence default to 0.5 and `f0_mean` to 0.0. This puts fake samples into the Pearson, CRQA and TE inputs, and `f0_mean` is the one most likely to be absent. Skip the sample for any series whose key is missing.

The window fallback `window_duration_ms` defaults to 30000, but `GroupDynamicsEngine` always emits `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` (60000). The fallback is misleading. The `deque(maxlen=60)` series comment says ~60 s, which only holds at one sample per second.
`logger` is unused. `import math` and `import logging` are out of alphabetical order. The `if composites else 0.5` fallback is dead, because at least two speakers means at least one pair.

Symmetry is 1.0 whenever both transfer entropies are 0. compute_transfer_entropy returns 0.0 for short series (under about 12 samples) and for constant series, so a snapshot with little data gets full symmetry credit, which is 0.20-0.25 of the composite. Return 0.0 or a neutral value when there isn't enough data to estimate TE.

Per-speaker series grow only when that speaker emits an event. _pearson_clamped, the CRQA input and the transfer-entropy input take the last n samples of each deque as if simultaneous, so they pair samples from different moments. Store timestamps and align the pair before correlating.

SERIES_MAXLEN=60 is labelled '~60s of 1 Hz' but only advances while a speaker is active, and the payload reports window_duration_ms from the snapshot (30 s). The reported window doesn't match the data used. Window by timestamp, or don't claim the duration.

When RunPod is unavailable, the local CRQA det (surrogate_validated=False) is used directly as coordination. Smooth f0 series give high recurrence by construction. The spec requires a noise-floor comparison or a TLCC fallback. Gate or discount unvalidated results.

A parallel per-speaker series store duplicates SpeakerTimeSeries (speaker.py), which already tracks per-speaker prosodic series and exposes speaker_ids() and get_f0_series(). Extend or reuse it instead of keeping a second store with different retention.

f0_mean defaults to 0.0 when absent, and unvoiced zeros are appended unfiltered, which skews z-scoring, CRQA and TE. Also, _local_compute is pure-Python O(n^2) per pair and runs on the event loop for every snapshot. Consider skipping missing/zero f0 and offloading with asyncio.to_thread.

_valence_proximity returns 1 - |mean_a - mean_b|, so two speakers who are both strongly negative (valence ~0) score positivity 1.0. That rewards shared negativity as 'positive'. Fold the valence level into the score, or rename the component to valence similarity.

Missing data inflates the composite. compute_symmetry returns 1.0 when both transfer-entropy values are 0 (fewer than ~12 samples, or constant f0). _valence_proximity falls back to 0.5. A pair with almost no data therefore gets about 0.2-0.25 from symmetry plus about 0.15 from positivity at meeting 1. Gate symmetry on enough samples, as _pearson_clamped does with its n < 3 check.
DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS = 30_000 conflicts with SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000 in dynamics.py, which is the real snapshot window. Import that constant instead of redefining it with a different value.

_handle_snapshot awaits _pair_rapport sequentially, and each call can wait up to runpod_timeout (4 s) on RunPod. With N speakers there are N(N-1)/2 pairs, so 4 speakers is up to 24 s blocking the EventBus handler. Run the pair computations concurrently with asyncio.gather.

No Orchestrator.attach_rapport_engine, unlike attach_emotion_correlator and attach_dynamics_engine. emotion/__init__.py does not export RapportEngine. Nothing in the repo can construct and subscribe the engine. Add both, or confirm the omission is intentional.

The `len(y_future) < _MIN_SAMPLES` guard is dead code. The earlier `n < lag + _MIN_SAMPLES` check already ensures `len(y_future) >= 2`. Remove it, or raise the floor so "too few usable samples after lagging" means something for the estimator.
The `ValueError` raises for `lag < 1` and `n_bins < 1` were not requested. They are harmless and prevent the empty-slice bug with `lag=0`, so keeping them is fine.

The `len(y_future) < _MIN_SAMPLES` guard is dead code. `len(y_future) == n - lag`, and the earlier `n < lag + _MIN_SAMPLES` check already returns 0.0 in exactly that case. Drop it, or replace it with a real 'too few usable samples' threshold if one was intended.

The new lowercase names sit between `GroupDynamicsEngine` and `PraatExtractor`, which breaks the otherwise alphabetical `__all__`. Move `compute_symmetry` and `compute_transfer_entropy` to the end, after `SpeakerTimeSeries`.

`lag = max(1, int(lag))` and `n_bins = max(2, int(n_bins))` silently change invalid arguments. `lag=0` quietly becomes 1 and returns a TE for a different lag than the caller asked for. Either raise `ValueError` or document the clamping in the docstring.

`__all__` is otherwise alphabetically sorted. The two new lowercase names are inserted between `GroupDynamicsEngine` and `PraatExtractor`, which breaks that order. Move them to the end of the list, which is also where isort-style sorting would put lowercase names.

`lag = max(1, int(lag))` and `n_bins = max(2, int(n_bins))` silently rewrite invalid arguments, so `lag=0` or `lag=-3` is treated as 1. The issue does not ask for this. A caller bug would be hidden and would return a plausible number. Either raise `ValueError` for `lag < 1` or `n_bins < 2`, or document the clamping in the docstring.

`_entropy_nats` builds a Python list, calls `cast("list[int]", ...)` only to satisfy the type checker, and then runs a Python-level loop. It is called 80+ times per TE call because of the 20 surrogates and 4 entropies each. Use `p = counts / n; return float(-(p * np.log(p)).sum())` instead. That drops the `cast` and the `math`/`typing` imports it needs, and it is vectorised.

The issue defines only short-series handling (return 0.0). The new `ValueError` raises for `lag < 1`, `n_bins < 1` and non-finite values are unrequested. The non-finite check also means a single NaN in a prosodic series, which may occur upstream, crashes the caller instead of returning a degraded value. Either drop these checks or confirm that the rapport caller handles the exceptions.

ValueError paths (lag<1, n_bins<1, non-finite values) are not in the spec. The finite-value check runs only after the short-series early return, so the same bad data gives 0.0 or an exception depending on length. Drop these or validate before the length check; the lag<1 check is arguably worth keeping.
`n < lag + 2 or n - lag < _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is partly redundant, because the second clause already implies the first at the current constant. Collapse to one condition or comment why both exist.
Sibling modules export their public API in __init__/__all__; compute_transfer_entropy and compute_symmetry are not exported. Optional.

Dropping non-finite pairs with a boolean mask and then lagging shifts later samples earlier, so the lag no longer matches the real time offset. TE is then computed on misaligned data without any signal. The handling is also unrequested scope. Remove it, or return 0.0 when non-finite values are present.

The public `n_bins` argument is silently capped to int((usable/4)**(1/3)), which is 3 for ~200 samples. The docstring doesn't say so, so callers passing n_bins=8 get something different. Document that `n_bins` is an upper bound.
The `n_bins <= 1` branch in `_discretize` is unreachable because the caller clamps to at least 2. Remove it.
`lag = max(int(lag), 1)` silently turns lag <= 0 into 1, which hides caller bugs. Raise ValueError for lag < 1, or document the coercion.

Dropping non-finite samples pairwise and then lagging the compacted arrays makes samples that were several steps apart look adjacent, so the result is no longer TE at the requested lag. The issue didn't ask for this handling. Remove it, or return 0.0 when non-finite values are present.
The cap on n_bins (about 3 bins at 200 samples) overrides the caller's value, including the default of 8, and the public docstring doesn't say so. Document that n_bins is an upper bound.

`_plugin_te` is called 31 times, but only `x` is permuted between calls. `h_fy` and `h_y` depend only on `y_future` and `y_past`, so they are identical every time. Recomputing them is avoidable work, and so is converting each permutation to a list. Compute the two terms once and have the surrogate loop compute only `h_fyx` and `h_yx`.

The issue does not ask for the `ValueError` on `n_bins < 2` or `lag < 1`. The `lag` check is defensible, because `y[:-0]` would silently return an empty slice. The `n_bins` check is extra, and a bad value would be an error anyway. The documented contract is to return 0.0 when there is too little data, so the new raise paths should be mentioned in the docstring. Also, `MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is public while the other constants are private, which is inconsistent.

The ValueError checks for lag < 1 and n_bins < 2 are not in the spec, and no other function in forgestream/emotion raises on bad arguments. Drop them or confirm raising is intended. Without them, lag=0 would hit an empty [:-0] slice.
MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES is public but the other module constants are underscore-private. Rename it to _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES unless callers need it.
The `n < lag + 2` check is implied by `n - lag < MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES`. It mirrors the spec, but a short comment would explain why both guards are there.

The ValueError checks for lag < 1, n_bins < 1 and non-finite input are not in the issue, which specifies returning 0.0 when the series can't be estimated. Raising on a NaN in live prosodic series conflicts with the project's never-reject-data stance. Drop the checks, or return 0.0 for non-finite input.

_CODE_BASE = 1 << 16 assumes n_bins <= 65536, but n_bins is only validated for >= 1. A larger n_bins would make the joint integer codes collide and silently give wrong entropies. Validate the upper bound or derive the base from n_bins.
`import math` is never used (the module uses numpy only). Remove it, since it will fail a lint check.

`_CODE_BASE = 1 << 16` assumes `n_bins` < 65536. A larger `n_bins` makes joint codes collide silently, and `n_bins` is only checked for `>= 1`. Either cap `n_bins` in the validation or use `np.unique(..., axis=0)` on stacked columns.

The `ValueError` checks for `lag < 1`, `n_bins < 1` and non-finite values are not in the issue. The non-finite check will raise on a NaN prosodic sample, where the caller probably expects 0.0 or a skipped sample. Check that callers want an exception here.
The `if n_bins < 2` branch in `_discretize` is unreachable. The only caller passes `k = max(2, int(n_bins))`. Remove the branch, or drop the clamp in the caller and keep the guard in one place.

`MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is public, but nothing outside this module uses it, and the other tuning constants (`_N_SHUFFLES`, `_BIAS_SEED`, `_EPSILON`) are underscore-private. Rename it to `_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` for consistency. Non-finite input also returns 0.0 silently. That is reasonable, but the docstring should say so.
Dead branch: `_discretize` handles `n_bins < 2`, but the only caller passes `k = max(2, int(n_bins))`, so that branch can never run. Remove it, or drop the clamp and keep the guard in one place.

Each of the 20 shuffle iterations recomputes `_entropy(yy)` and `_entropy(y_past)` via `_plugin_te_nats`. Neither depends on `x_past`, so they are identical every time. Hoist them out of the loop and recompute only `H(yy_x)` and `H(yp_x)` per shuffle. This halves the surrogate cost without changing the results.

The `lag < 1` and `n_bins < 2` ValueError checks aren't in the spec. The spec only says to return 0.0 when the series are too short. Raising here is a new failure mode that a caller feeding live speaker data now has to handle. Either keep it and document it in the spec, or drop it. Note that lag=0 would otherwise index y[-1:...] and silently produce garbage, so the guard has some value.

In `_plugin_te`, `c_yp` is just an alias for `y_prev`, and `b` aliases `n_bins`. Use `y_prev` directly in the `_entropy_bits` call and drop the alias. The `te` temporary is also unnecessary; return the expression directly.

Each call runs 21 plug-in TE estimates (1 observed plus 20 surrogates), with a hidden fixed seed. This is fine for the stated use, but `_N_SURROGATES` and the seed are not parameters. If this will run inside the 60s dynamics loop for many speaker pairs, the cost should be measured. The module docstring should also say that the result is bias-corrected TE, not the raw plug-in value.

`if usable < 2: return 0.0` is dead code: `n < lag + 2` already returned, so `usable = n - lag >= 2` always holds. The 'too few usable samples after lagging' case from the issue is therefore not actually handled. Remove it or use a real minimum-sample threshold.

`te_for` returns H(Yp,X) - H(Yf,Yp,X) = -H(Yf|Yp,X), not TE. The comment 'the Yf,Yp and Yp terms are shared' hides that terms were dropped, and the result is only correct because the surrogate difference cancels them. Rename it and state the cancellation explicitly.

Silent 0.0 for lag < 1, n_bins < 2 and non-finite input is unrequested and hides caller bugs. NaN looks the same as 'no influence'. Consider raising ValueError for bad parameters, or document the NaN behaviour.

Bias is corrected twice, by Miller-Madow in `_entropy_bits` and by the shuffled-source surrogate subtraction. The surrogate step already removes the bias, so Miller-Madow looks redundant. Drop it or justify it in the docstring.

`te_for` is not transfer entropy. It returns `H(Yp,X) - H(Yf,Yp,X)`, which equals `-H(Yf|Yp,X)` and is always <= 0. It only gives a valid TE once the constant `H(Yf|Yp)` term cancels in the `te_for(xb) - surrogate` subtraction. The comment 'the Yf,Yp and Yp terms are shared' is easy to misread. Rename it to something like `neg_cond_entropy` and say that the result is the real value minus the surrogate mean, so the dropped term cancels.

The Miller-Madow correction in `_entropy_bits` and the shuffled-surrogate subtraction both correct small-sample bias. The surrogate step already removes the bias, and the Miller-Madow terms mostly cancel in the difference. Drop Miller-Madow to remove a redundant, hard-to-justify term, or document why both are needed.

The 'too few usable samples' guard is only `usable < 2`. With 2 to about 10 usable samples, the 8-bin joint histogram (8^3 cells) is almost all singletons. The surrogate-corrected value is then noise, though clipping at 0 keeps it non-negative. Use a more meaningful minimum, such as a multiple of `n_bins`. Otherwise short windows can yield spurious non-zero TE, which would feed into the symmetry score.

The `n_usable < _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` check and the `_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES = 2` constant are dead code. The earlier `n < lag + 2` guard already ensures `n - lag >= 2`. Remove them, or set a real minimum if "too few usable samples" is meant to be stricter.
The package `__init__` re-exports every public symbol. Add `compute_transfer_entropy` and `compute_symmetry` to the imports and `__all__` so they match the rest of the module.

The `n_usable < _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` check is dead code. `n >= lag + 2` is already enforced above, so `n_usable = n - lag >= 2`. Remove the check and the `_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` constant, or fold the requirement into the first guard.
`__init__.py` re-exports every other public emotion component via `__all__`. `compute_transfer_entropy` and `compute_symmetry` are not added, so the new public API is inconsistent with its siblings.

`n_bins` is only floored at 2, with no upper bound. `_entropy_bits` allocates `np.bincount` over `n_bins**3` codes, so a large value (e.g. 1000 gives 1e9 slots) allocates gigabytes. Past roughly 2e6 bins the int64 code overflows. Cap `n_bins`, for example to a small multiple of `sqrt(n)`, or compute the joint codes with `np.unique`.

`compute_symmetry` jumps from 1.0 to 0.0 at the `_EPS` threshold. Inputs like (1e-8, 0) give 0.0 while (1e-10, 0) gives 1.0. The surrogate-corrected TE is often exactly 0 in one direction and tiny noise in the other, so near-zero pairs will score 0.0. A larger epsilon, or damping the score when the total is small, would avoid this. Acceptable if the spec only asks for the 'effectively zero' special case.

The `n < lag + 2` check is subsumed by `n - lag < MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES`, since MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES is 10. Merge the two checks or note that the first is kept for spec parity. `MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is the only public-style constant here; the other constants are underscore-prefixed.

`_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` and the `usable < _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` check are dead code. `n >= lag + 2` already guarantees `usable = n - lag >= 2`. Remove the constant and the second guard, or make the minimum meaningful. With 2 usable samples against 8 bins the estimate is not meaningful anyway.

Both `compute_transfer_entropy` calls (A→B and B→A) run the plug-in estimator 21 times, each using four Python `Counter` passes over `.tolist()` lists. That is fine for short windows. It is wasteful if called every 60s on long series. Either encode the joint states as ints and use `np.unique`/`bincount`, or note the expected series length in the docstring. Also, non-finite input and `lag<1` silently return 0.0, which conflates 'no influence' with 'bad input'. The docstring only mentions the short-series case.

The `usable < _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` branch and the `_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` constant are dead code. The previous guard `n < lag + 2` already guarantees `usable = n - lag >= 2`. Drop them, or make the threshold larger than the length guard so it does something. A TE estimate from 2 samples is meaningless, so the 'too few usable samples' case from the issue is not really covered.

`_entropy_bits` repeats the Shannon-entropy loop in `EmotionDynamics.compute_turn_taking_entropy` in `dynamics.py`. The two differ slightly (that one normalizes and guards `p > 0`), so sharing a helper would need a small refactor. Acceptable as is, but a shared plug-in entropy helper would avoid two copies.
MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES is public while the other module constants are underscore-private. Nothing outside the module needs it, so make it _MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES.
The new public functions aren't exported from forgestream/emotion/__init__.py like the other emotion components. This is optional now; add them when the rapport scorer starts importing them.

Unrequested validation: ValueError for lag<1 and n_bins<1, and a silent 0.0 return for non-finite input. The lag<1 guard is defensible, since yb[:-0] would produce empty slices. The NaN/inf case returns 0.0 and hides bad upstream features. Remove or document these.
MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES lacks the leading underscore that the other module constants (_EPSILON, _N_SURROGATES, _SURROGATE_SEED) have, though all are module-internal. Make the naming consistent.
The final max(0.0, min(1.0, ...)) clamp in compute_symmetry is redundant, because a and b are already clamped to >= 0, so |a-b|/total is in [0, 1]. Drop it.
`__all__` is sorted and the new `compute_symmetry` / `compute_transfer_entropy` entries are inserted out of order (between `EGeMAPSExtractor` and `EmotionCorpus`). Move them to sorted position.

Non-finite input silently returns 0.0 and `lag < 1` / `n_bins < 2` raise `ValueError`. Neither is in the spec. A NaN in a prosodic series would read as "no influence" rather than being filtered or surfaced. Document both behaviours in the docstring, or drop the non-finite shortcut.

`__all__` is alphabetically sorted. The new lowercase `compute_symmetry` and `compute_transfer_entropy` entries are wedged between `EGeMAPSExtractor` and `EmotionCorpus`. Move them to the end so the ordering stays consistent.

The issue specifies the return-0.0 cases for short input, but not a `ValueError` for `lag < 1` or `n_bins < 2`. It also does not say to return 0.0 for NaN or inf input. The non-finite branch hides bad upstream features as 'no influence'. The 0.0 also feeds `compute_symmetry`, which turns it into a perfect-symmetry score. Either drop both checks, or raise on non-finite input rather than returning a plausible-looking 0.0.
`MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is public but `_EPS` and `_N_SURROGATES` are private. Nothing outside the module uses it, so make it `_MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES`.

`_effective_bins` silently overrides the caller's `n_bins`. At the 200-sample size in the spec, the default 8 becomes 4, and any larger value is ignored too. The signature and docs promise `n_bins` bins, so a caller who passes an explicit value gets a different discretisation. The module docstring describes the cap, but the `compute_transfer_entropy` docstring does not. Say there that `n_bins` is an upper bound, or expose the capping behaviour, so results stay predictable.

`y_future.tolist()`, `y_past.tolist()` and `x_past.tolist()` are each computed two or three times. Compute them once into locals. The quotes around the `Counter[...]` annotation in `_entropy_mm` are also redundant, because `from __future__ import annotations` is already imported.

The comment `t in [max(lag,1), n)` is stale. `lag >= 1` is already enforced, so it should read `[lag, n)`. `start = lag` is also redundant. `x_p` is the lagged source and `y_p` is the target's past, so the names are easy to confuse. Consider `x_lagged` and `y_prev`.

The `ValueError` for `lag < 1` or `n_bins < 1` wasn't requested, but it is reasonable. `_entropy(counts: Counter, ...)` also uses a bare `Counter`. Annotate it as `Counter[Any]`, or accept an iterable of counts, to match typed usage elsewhere.
The comment `for t in [max(lag,1), n)` is stale. `lag >= 1` is enforced above, so `start = lag` and the `max(lag,1)` wording is misleading. Say `t in [lag, n)`.

The surrogate loop calls `_plugin_te` on each pass, so it recomputes `H(f,yp)` and `H(yp)`, which don't depend on the shuffled `x`. That is 2 of 4 `np.unique` sorts wasted per surrogate. Compute them once, then recompute only `H(yp,x)` and `H(f,yp,x)` per permutation.

The issue doesn't ask for the silent `return 0.0` on non-finite input. It can hide NaN/inf from upstream feature extraction as 'no influence'. Drop it or document it. The `ValueError` for lag/n_bins < 1 is also unrequested but reasonable.
`import math` is unused. Every logarithm goes through `np.log2`. Remove the import.

Clamping effective TE at 0 means weak but real coupling below the surrogate bias returns 0.0. compute_symmetry then maps (0, 0) to 1.0, which is the same result as a pair with no influence at all. Document in the docstring that 0.0 means "not distinguishable from noise", and that symmetry is therefore uninformative when both TE values are 0.

The `n < lag + 2` check is already covered by `n - lag < MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES`. The non-finite-input early return is also unrequested and undocumented. Drop the redundant condition and mention the NaN/inf behaviour in the docstring.

The issue doesn't ask for the `ValueError` on non-finite input or on `lag < 1` / `n_bins < 2`, and it only defines a `0.0` return for short series. Prosodic series such as F0 contours commonly contain NaN for unvoiced frames, so raising here would crash a rapport-scoring caller on ordinary data. Either drop the non-finite check or handle NaN by returning `0.0`, and document whichever you choose. The `lag` and `n_bins` guards are acceptable but not required.

`compute_transfer_entropy` returns an effective TE (plug-in estimate minus a mean over 20 shuffled-source surrogates, clamped at 0), not the TE the function name and the issue describe. The clamp also hides real but weak influence. The deviation is documented in the module docstring, but the public function docstring should say that the value is bias-corrected and floored at 0, so callers don't compare it to textbook TE values.

Raising ValueError on non-finite input is unrequested and breaks the neighbouring convention. dynamics.py compute_* helpers return neutral values on degenerate input, and features.py clamps NaN to 0. Prosodic series (e.g. F0) can contain NaN, so one NaN would make this throw inside the periodic dynamics computation. Drop the check, or return 0.0 or filter non-finite samples, consistent with the 'too few usable samples -> 0.0' contract. The lag/n_bins raises are also unrequested, though defensible.

`n < lag + 2` is dead code: it implies `n - lag < 2`, which `n - lag < MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` already catches. Keep one condition. `MIN_USABLE_SAMPLES` is also public while the other constants are `_`-prefixed; make it private unless it is meant to be API.

`_plugin_te_nats` is called 20 times for the surrogates, and each call recomputes `H(y_future, y_past)` and `H(y_past)`. Neither depends on the shuffled `x_past`. Compute them once and only redo the two x-dependent terms per surrogate. `np.unique(..., axis=0)` on a stacked array is also slow. Encoding the columns into a single int64 key would be cheaper. This matters once it runs repeatedly over a rolling window.

The issue does not ask for the `ValueError` on `lag < 1` or `n_bins < 1`, or for the silent `0.0` on NaN/inf input. Returning `0.0` for non-finite data hides bad upstream features as 'no influence'. Either keep it and document it in the docstring, or drop it.
The `n - lag < 2` guard is redundant. `n >= lag + 2` already implies `n - lag >= 2`. Drop it. The `lag < 1 or n_bins < 1` cases silently return 0.0; that is acceptable, but note it in the docstring.
`n - lag < 2` is the same condition as `n < lag + 2` (algebraically equivalent), so the second check is redundant. Drop it.

`lag` is not validated. For `lag < 1`, `m = len(x) - lag` and the slices `y[lag:]` / `y[:m]` misalign when `lag` is negative, so the entropies are normalised by the wrong `m` and the result is silent garbage.
